entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text:
The claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the IV Additional District and Sessions Judge at Vijayapur in MVC No.702/2014, vide its judgment and award dated 27.11.2015.
2.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge at Vijayapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claimant claimed that he was the owner of an autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-29/A-3852 which was damaged in a road traffic accident on 07.02.2014 when a tipper lorry bearing registration No.KA-33/A-2180 rear ended it.
The claimant therefore filed a claim petition claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the tipper for the damages caused to the autorickshaw, which was assessed at a sum of Rs.1,34,972/-.
He also claimed loss of earning since the repair of the autorickshaw took nearly 87 days.
The claim petition was contested by the insurer who denied the accident as well as the damages caused to the autorickshaw.
However, it contended that the autorickshaw was carrying more passengers than it permitted and that it was the driver of the autorickshaw who was negligent.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.2 and documents were commonly marked with the claimants in the other claim petitions.

The police inspector was examined as RW.1 and a copy of the policy of insurance was marked as Ex.R1.
5.

Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal noticed Ex.P4 which was the report of the motor vehicle inspector which indicated the following damages to the autorickshaw:
1. Front wind screen glass was dislocated from its place.
2. Right side headlight was dislocated from its place.

sentences.text: Left side of the bottom body was brokered and pressed inwards.
4. Seats are damaged.
5. Rear both wheel were damaged.
6. Rear left side axle was brokened.
6. It considered Ex.P9 which was the estimate produced by the claimant and held that the claimant did not produce any material to indicate that a sum of Rs.1,34,972/- was paid to the repairer.

The Tribunal therefore assessed the cost of repair at a sum of Rs.20,000/- and the loss of income at a sum of Rs.4,000/- during the idling period and awarded a sum of Rs.24,000/- as compensation and directed the insurer to pay the same along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from date of claim petition till the date of realization.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation, the claimant is in appeal.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant contended that though the photographs placed on record as per Exs.P10, P11 and P12 showing the extent of NC: 2023:KHC-K:5444 damages caused to the autorickshaw which corresponded to the estimate at Ex.P9, the Tribunal committed an error in ignoring the cost of repair.
He submitted that the Tribunal had no knowledge about the cost incurred for the repair.

He submitted that Ex.P9 was the estimate prepared by Anushree Enterprise,
Vijayapur and there was no evidence by the insurer to deny the correctness of the estimation.
8. The learned counsel for the insurer on the other hand contended that the autorickshaw was manufactured in the year 2011 while the accident in question happened on 07.02.2014.
He submitted that the damages were rightly noticed by the Motor Vehicle Inspector as per Ex.P4 and cost of repair was rightly assessed by the Tribunal and therefore, the appeal may be dismissed.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant as well as the learned counsel for the respondent/insurer.
The photographs placed on record as per Exs.P10, 11 and 12 indicate that the front wind screen glass was dislocated from its place and rear wheels were damaged and chassis was also broken.
Therefore, it could be quite possible that other parts were also damaged and the estimate at Ex.P9 nearly corresponded to the damages caused to the autorickshaw.
The insurer did not adduce any evidence to indicate that the estimate at Ex.P9 was without any basis.

11. In that view of the matter, this Court considers it appropriate to award a sum of Rs.70,000/-
towards cost of repair and a sum of Rs.22,500/- being the loss of income during idling period of three months as the vehicle took nearly 87 days for its repair.

sentences.text:
In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part and the compensation of Rs.24,000/-
determined by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.92,500/-.

The enhanced compensation of Rs.68,500/- shall be paid by the insurer to the claimant along with interest at NC: 2023:KHC-K:5444 the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment and award.
